stories.title: 'We have listened': SRA proposes major SQE adjustments
stories.ltme_summary: The Solicitors Regulation Authority has proposed major changes to the Solicitors Qualifying Examination, according to the regulator's announcement on 19 November. Under the consultation, candidates could sit the two parts of SQE1 on separate days, the cap of three resits would be removed, and the six-year validity clock would start when a candidate passes an assessment. The consultation closes on 11 February and changes would take effect in 2028.
stories.hook: SRA proposes splitting SQE1 across days and removing the resit cap, with changes due in 2028.

stories.title: Lawyer banned from ECtHR after using AI to draft submissions
stories.ltme_summary: The European Court of Human Rights has barred a Romanian lawyer from representing applicants before the court for two years. The chamber found that submissions she drafted with AI contained non-existent cases and misused authorities, and that the errors had forced the court to spend considerable time verifying them. The lawyer, not named by the court, admitted using AI tools and the chamber found her conduct met the exceptional circumstances threshold under Rule 44D.
stories.hook: ECtHR bars a Romanian lawyer for two years after AI-drafted observations cited non-existent cases.

stories.title: Competence in an AI world: not just an early-career problem

Half of participants outperformed the AI working alone. The authors argue the lessons apply to lawyers, citing SRA and BSB competence standards.

stories.title: Law firm fails in appeal against £60k fine for major data breach
stories.ltme_summary: The First-tier Tribunal has dismissed DPP Law's appeal against a £60,000 fine imposed by the Information Commissioner's Office after a 2022 cyber attack exposed data on 682 clients. The tribunal found the firm's failings were negligent and that the penalty was justified as a deterrent to other law firms relying on external suppliers. DPP notified the regulator 43 days after the attack.
stories.hook: Tribunal upholds £60,000 ICO fine on DPP Law, saying the deterrent figure was justified

stories.title: Less pressure, more resits – SRA outlines further SQE reforms

Proposals include letting candidates sit the two functioning legal knowledge assessments separately, unlimited resits, and starting the six-year qualification window from the date a candidate first passes an assessment. Question numbers fall to 170 from 1 January 2027.
stories.hook: SRA consults on unlimited SQE resits and separate sittings of FLK1 and FLK2
